questions.question_text: Which ingredient makes a cake rise by giving off gas in the oven?
questions.explanation: Baking powder releases gas when it is wet and heated, so the batter puffs up.
traps: Salt and sugar do not make a cake rise.

questions.question_text: Sugar in a cake only adds sweetness and does nothing else.
questions.explanation: Sugar also helps the cake brown, keeps it moist and makes it tender.
traps: Sugar does more than sweeten.

questions.question_text: What is the main ingredient in a meringue?
questions.explanation: Whisked egg whites hold air bubbles, which makes a meringue light and crisp.
traps: Butter and flour are not used in a plain meringue.

questions.question_text: Chilling cookie dough before baking can help the cookies keep their shape.
questions.explanation: Cold butter melts more slowly, so the cookies spread less.
traps: Chilling does not make the dough rise.

questions.question_text: What does beating butter and sugar together until fluffy do?
questions.explanation: Creaming traps tiny air bubbles, which help the cake rise and feel light.
traps: The sugar does not melt at this stage.

questions.question_text: Vanilla flavouring comes from the pods of a type of orchid.
questions.explanation: Vanilla beans are the cured pods of an orchid, Vanilla planifolia.
traps: Vanilla is not made from a bean of coffee.

questions.question_text: Ice cream is made by freezing a sweet cream mixture while doing what?
questions.explanation: Stirring, or churning, breaks up ice crystals and keeps the ice cream smooth.
traps: Leaving ice cream still makes it icy.

questions.question_text: Baking soda needs an acid, such as buttermilk or lemon juice, to make bubbles.
questions.explanation: Baking soda is a base. It makes gas only when an acid is present.
traps: Baking soda on its own does not make a cake rise well.

questions.question_text: What is a custard mainly made of?
choices: Eggs, milk or cream, and sugar
questions.correct_answer: Eggs, milk or cream, and sugar
questions.explanation: Eggs thicken the milk or cream as they gently cook.
traps: Flour is not the base of a classic custard.

questions.question_text: Which sugar is the plain white sugar most often used in baking?
questions.explanation: Granulated sugar is the everyday white sugar in most recipes.
traps: Brown sugar has molasses in it.

questions.question_text: Brown sugar contains molasses.
questions.explanation: Molasses is what gives brown sugar its colour and a soft, rich taste.
traps: Brown sugar is not just white sugar with colour added.

questions.question_text: What does folding mean in baking?
choices: Gently mixing with a spatula to keep the air in
Beating very hard with a whisk
Heating the mixture until it boils
questions.correct_answer: Gently mixing with a spatula to keep the air in
questions.explanation: Folding moves ingredients together slowly, so the air stays in a light batter.
traps: Beating hard knocks the air out.

questions.question_text: Which fruit is used in the classic French upside-down tart, the tarte Tatin?
questions.explanation: Apples are cooked in butter and sugar, then the pastry is placed on top and the tart is turned out.
traps: Lemons are used in lemon curd, not in tarte Tatin.

questions.question_text: A pavlova is a dessert built around a meringue base.
questions.explanation: A pavlova is a crisp meringue shell, often topped with cream and fruit.
traps: A pavlova is not a sponge cake.

questions.question_text: What is a crumble topping usually made from?
questions.explanation: Rubbing cold butter into flour and sugar makes the crumbly topping.
traps: Crumble is not made with eggs.

questions.question_text: Mixing a muffin batter too much can make the muffins tough.
questions.explanation: Too much mixing builds up gluten, which makes baked goods chewy and tough.
traps: Muffins should be mixed only until just combined.

questions.question_text: What is a ganache made from?
questions.explanation: Stirring hot cream into chocolate makes a smooth, glossy ganache.
traps: Ganache is not made with flour.

questions.question_text: Why do recipes often say to preheat the oven?
choices: So the oven is at the right heat when the food goes in
So the oven can cool down first
questions.correct_answer: So the oven is at the right heat when the food goes in
questions.explanation: A hot oven starts the rising and setting straight away, which gives a better bake.
traps: Preheating is not for cooling the oven.

questions.question_text: Lemon curd is made from eggs, sugar, butter and lemon juice.
questions.explanation: Lemon curd is cooked gently until thick, using eggs, sugar, butter and lemon.
traps: Lemon curd does not need flour.

questions.question_text: Which Italian dessert is made with layers of ladyfinger biscuits and mascarpone cream?
questions.explanation: Tiramisu is soaked in coffee and layered with a creamy mascarpone mixture.
traps: A pavlova is made with meringue, not ladyfingers.

questions.question_text: A cheesecake is never chilled after it is baked.
questions.explanation: Many cheesecakes are baked, then cooled and chilled so they set firmly.
traps: Cheesecake is often chilled to set it.

questions.question_text: Why is a cake often left to rest before it is sliced?
choices: It firms up so it does not crumble
questions.correct_answer: It firms up so it does not crumble
questions.explanation: As it cools, the cake sets, so it holds together when cut.
traps: Resting does not add sweetness.

questions.question_text: What is sorbet mainly made of?
questions.explanation: Sorbet is a fruit ice with no milk or cream.
traps: Sorbet does not contain milk.

questions.question_text: Brownies are usually made with cocoa or chocolate.
questions.explanation: Cocoa or melted chocolate gives brownies their rich flavour.
traps: Brownies are not usually made with vanilla alone.

questions.question_text: Why are baked custards often cooked in a water bath?
choices: It cooks them gently so they do not curdle
questions.correct_answer: It cooks them gently so they do not curdle
questions.explanation: The water keeps the heat gentle and even, so the eggs set smoothly.
traps: A water bath does not make custard rise.

questions.question_text: Why should a cake batter go into the oven soon after the baking powder is stirred in?
choices: Baking powder starts making bubbles as soon as it is wet
Baking powder stops working in the oven
Baking powder needs to be cooked first
The batter goes flat if it is stirred
questions.correct_answer: Baking powder starts making bubbles as soon as it is wet
questions.explanation: Once wet, baking powder begins releasing gas, so waiting too long wastes some of its lift.
traps: It is not that the cake needs to sit first.

questions.question_text: A soufflé falls if the oven door is opened too early. Why?
choices: Cold air rushes in and the rising air bubbles collapse
The eggs are cooked too much
The soufflé gets too heavy to stand
questions.correct_answer: Cold air rushes in and the rising air bubbles collapse
questions.explanation: Sudden cold air shrinks the hot air and steam inside, so the soufflé loses its rise.
traps: Eggs are not the reason it falls when the door is opened early.

questions.question_text: Caramel turns brown because sugar breaks down and changes colour as it is heated.
questions.explanation: As sugar heats past its melting point, it changes chemically and turns golden then brown.
traps: Caramel does not turn brown from milk alone.

questions.question_text: Sam's cake came out flat and sank in the middle. The baking powder was fresh, the flour was measured, and the oven was working. Which change would most likely fix it?
choices: Bake it a little longer and keep the oven door closed until it is nearly set
Open the oven door every minute to check it
Add more baking soda without any acid
Beat the batter for much longer
questions.correct_answer: Bake it a little longer and keep the oven door closed until it is nearly set
questions.explanation: A cake that sinks in the middle is often underbaked or was disturbed while rising, so a longer, undisturbed bake helps it set.
traps: Opening the door early can make a cake sink, and so can beating it too long.

questions.question_text: Which two steps together make homemade ice cream smoother and less icy?
choices: Churn while it freezes, and add a little sugar or alcohol to keep ice crystals small
Freeze it still and never stir it
Add extra water and freeze it solid
Heat it to boiling before freezing
questions.correct_answer: Churn while it freezes, and add a little sugar or alcohol to keep ice crystals small
questions.explanation: Churning breaks up ice crystals, and sugar or alcohol lowers the freezing point, so fewer large icy crystals form.
traps: Standing still freezing makes icier ice cream.
